clue.text: French stamp offers sound quality

definitions.meaning: the French word for a postage stamp
the tone colour that distinguishes one voice or instrument from another

explanation.surface: A French postage stamp somehow carries a fine tone.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a postage stamp is also English for the characteristic tone colour of a voice.

clue.text: Spring exhibition in London

definitions.note: the definition names a place found in London: the upmarket district in the West End

parts.note: May is a month of spring
a fair is a show or exhibition

explanation.surface: A springtime show is being staged in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a district of London's West End, and 'in London' points to where it is.
explanation.definitionFit: The district is a wealthy area of central London's West End.

clue.text: Guardian produced a discount scheme

indicators.note: to scheme is to plot or arrange, so the letters of the words before are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A newspaper or protector has come up with a money-off offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' tempts as the newspaper, but it is the keeper. 'produced' is a link; 'scheme' rearranges A DISCOUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper or warden is someone who has guardianship of something.

clue.text: A little sweet

definitions.meaning: a small, insignificant amount
a British cold dessert of sponge, fruit, custard and cream

explanation.walkthrough: The British dessert is layers of sherry-soaked sponge, fruit, custard and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A small amount and a layered British pudding share the same name.

clue.text: Husband and father

definitions.meaning: informal word for a woman's spouse
informal word for one's dad

explanation.definitionFit: Both a spouse and a dad are informally called this two-word phrase.

clue.text: Twice concluded that it is exaggerated

parts.note: something concluded is over
something concluded is also done

explanation.surface: Saying it ended twice suggests an overstatement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twice concluded' asks for two different words for finished, placed side by side; 'that it is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An overacted or overstated performance is described as taken too far.

clue.text: Bill made a sketch

definitions.meaning: a bank ... is a written order to pay, a bill of exchange
a rough preliminary version of a drawing or document

explanation.surface: Bill has drawn something.
explanation.definitionFit: A banker's order for payment and a rough first version share one name.

clue.text: A summary difficult to understand

definitions.meaning: a short précis of a paper or article
theoretical and hard to grasp

explanation.definitionFit: An academic précis and something hard to grasp, being theoretical, share one word.

clue.text: Urinary disorder spread round the hospital fast

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are spread round a piece placed inside them
a disorder throws the letters of the word before into confusion

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A medical complaint of the waterworks affects someone in a ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' looks medical but scrambles URINARY to INAURRY; 'spread round' puts H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone moving quickly or rushing is said to be hasty.

clue.text: A leper's treatment has clearly failed!

definitions.text: A leper's treatment has clearly failed!

indicators.note: treatment works the letters of the words before into a new form

explanation.surface: A leprosy patient's therapy has evidently not worked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' rearranges the letters of A LEPERS; read whole, a cured patient falling ill again is exactly what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: A return of illness after apparent recovery shows that treatment did not hold.

clue.text: Look after your health: that has to be right

definitions.meaning: split as two words, keep in good shape
to be suitable or proper for

explanation.surface: Staying healthy is the proper thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the word urges keeping in shape; as one word it means to suit or be appropriate.

clue.text: Eulogistic declaration that old archbishop was a Conservative

parts.note: William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A tribute claims a former primate was a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: William Laud, Archbishop of Canterbury executed in 1645, is the old archbishop; 'declaration that' and 'was' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A eulogy praises, so something eulogistic is full of praise.

clue.text: Member urging militaristic policy

definitions.meaning: a limb of the body
to equip with weapons, as a verb one might urge in favour of war

explanation.definitionFit: A limb and the verb for supplying weapons share one word.

clue.text: O deliver reformed sinner

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plea to save a sinner who has changed his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' looks like a description of the sinner, but it rearranges O DELIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer or wicked person is a sinner.

clue.text: Observe that the water hasn't frozen

definitions.meaning: to see or spot
split in two, the water is not yet solid

explanation.surface: Someone sees that the pond has not iced over.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to observe it; split, the word says the water is unfrozen.

clue.text: Quite frankly, Mr McEnroe, the service was good

definitions.meaning: to speak plainly

definitions.text: Mr McEnroe, the service was good
definitions.meaning: John McEnroe, the tennis player, famously disputed line calls

explanation.surface: A line judge tells the tennis star his serve counted.
explanation.walkthrough: John McEnroe was a tennis player notorious for disputing calls; a serve touching the line is good.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking plainly is laying it on the line, and a ball touching the boundary is in.

clue.text: Minor Oxbridge sportsman alternately happy and sad

definitions.meaning: an award for representing Oxford or Cambridge in a lesser sport
blue means sad, so being sad only half the time

explanation.surface: A second-tier university athlete has mixed feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge a full blue is awarded for major sports, a lesser award for minor ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxbridge awards a reduced colours award for minor sports; read literally, it is being down only half the time.

clue.text: Meet for a games lesson

parts.note: PT is physical training, a school sports lesson

explanation.surface: A gathering for a PE class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meet' is the old adjective meaning fitting, not a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Meet is an archaic word for suitable or fitting.

clue.text: Dad's game to take on a trip abroad

definitions.text: to take on a trip abroad

parts.note: pa is dad, so dad's is pa's
a sport is a game

explanation.surface: Father's favourite pastime is something to bring on holiday overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's of 'Dad's' supplies a real S here.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel document is what one carries when going to another country.

clue.text: Know Livingstone?

definitions.meaning: a Scottish verb for to know
the first name of the former Mayor of London Livingstone

explanation.surface: Is someone acquainted with the explorer Livingstone?
explanation.walkthrough: Livingstone is the London mayor, not the explorer David.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots verb for knowing matches the first name of London's first elected mayor.

clue.text: Guy must get two articles later

parts.note: a guy is a man
an is the indefinite article
a is the indefinite article too

explanation.surface: A man must pick up a couple of newspaper pieces at some point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must get' is a link; 'articles' are grammar, not newspaper pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for tomorrow is used in English for some vague time in the future.

clue.text: Letter greeting gives support to the President

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece giving support sits below the one it holds up

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for President
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A welcome note backs the head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek character is a letter of an alphabet.

clue.text: Country genius full of sex appeal

indicators.note: full of means the first piece holds the second

parts.note: a brain is a clever person
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A brilliant mind is also very attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex appeal comes from the 1920s 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: The nation of England, Scotland and Wales is a country.

clue.text: Dolichocephalic culture-vulture

definitions.meaning: long-headed, read literally as having a tall forehead
an intellectual devoted to the arts

explanation.definitionFit: An intellectual is one, and a long-headed person literally has a tall forehead.

clue.text: One does business with perfect models

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
deals means trades

explanation.surface: Someone trades in flawless mannequins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link; 'models' are standards of perfection, not fashion models.
explanation.definitionFit: Standards of perfection to aim at are perfect examples.

clue.text: Injustices which are never right

definitions.meaning: unjust acts
things always incorrect

explanation.surface: Unfair acts can never be correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Unjust acts are harms, and things never correct are incorrect ones.

clue.text: A warning of course was given, as stated

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout on a golf course
said means was uttered or given out

explanation.surface: A caution was issued on the golf course, as reported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' is a golf course, where a player shouts a warning to others.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mentioned earlier is previously stated.

clue.text: Schemes of benefit in the Royal Society

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: RS stands for the Royal Society
use is benefit or advantage

explanation.surface: Plans for perks at the learned society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tricks or stratagems are cunning schemes.

clue.text: Chance to win a gamble

definitions.meaning: a lottery game offering a chance of a prize
a game of chance with numbered cards

explanation.surface: An opportunity of winning a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A numbers game is a lottery: a prize draw and a wager.

clue.text: Flowers in flower after the vessel has been removed

indicators.note: in places the vessel within the flower

parts.note: a bloom is a flower
SS is a steamship

explanation.surface: Flowers bloom once the vase has been taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards: removing the vessel from the answer leaves the flower, so the phrase 'after the vessel has been removed' is the setter's way of saying the vessel sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The mass of flowers on a tree or bush is its flowering.

clue.text: Rattling a Scottish sovereign

parts.note: a clan is a Scottish family group
a king is a sovereign

explanation.surface: Unsettling a monarch of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rattling' looks like 'unsettling' but means making a metallic noise; a clan is a Highland Scottish kin group.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattling sound is metallic clattering.

clue.text: Socialite returns to take a seat in the living room

indicators.note: returns means the word for the socialite is read backwards

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young socialite
sit means take a seat

explanation.surface: A society girl comes back to sit down in the lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'in the' are links; a British one-room flat combines bedroom and sitting room.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-room flat serving as both bedroom and sitting room is a single living room.
